_comment: DATA_MODEL.md 「本文の形式」 (M189, 2026-11-16): how an input's `@name` becomes the stored token when a message is sent or saved after editing and when a canvas is saved, the same on every client (mentions.ts encodeMentions, Mentions.swift Mentions.encode, Mentions.kt Mentions.encode). A handle is `@` and ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`, at the start or after anything but those, `@` or `<` (an e-mail address and a stored `<@id>` stay as they are), also with the `_` that opens italic in between (`_@name_`; not after a letter or digit, where `_` opens no italic). Names compare without case; `@channel` / `@here` are `<!channel>` / `<!here>`. The longest known name wins: when the whole handle is no one's, a `.`, `_` or `-` at its end is left out one at a time and stays after the token (`@name.` ending a sentence, `_確認 @name_` closing italic; editing such a message turned its mention into text before M189), a letter or digit never is. An unknown handle stays text. users / groups: [id, name].

cases.name: italic around here and a group
a name ending with _ is the whole handle first
a letter or digit is never left out
no italic after a letter or digit
